painting.style: A painting in the Bengal School manner of the 1920s, in the lineage of Abanindranath Tagore and Nandalal Bose, drawing on Mughal and Pahari miniature convention. Flat opaque colour with no cast shadows and no chiaroscuro. A high or absent horizon and no perspective of any kind: no vanishing point, no receding ground plane, no atmospheric haze, no diminishing scale with distance. The scene is built in flat stacked bands, near figures simply lower on the sheet and far figures higher, all at much the same size. Figures in profile or three-quarter view, drawn with a fine brush; hierarchical scale, with the important figure larger. Architecture shown in plan and elevation at once. Modelling by fine brush stipple rather than blending. A ruled decorative border framing the composition. Palette of lapis and ultramarine, vermilion, orpiment yellow, malachite green, white lead and gold leaf, laid flat and unmixed. Subject:
painting.constraints: Painted on paper, matte, slightly aged. No photographic realism, no photograph, no 3D render, no digital airbrush, no lens blur, no depth of field, no dramatic lighting, no perspective recession, no vanishing point, no atmospheric perspective, no soft focus in the distance. No text, no lettering, no calligraphy, no signature, no watermark, no border captions.

kalighat.style: A Kalighat pat from Calcutta, about 1920 — a cheap devotional print painted in minutes for sale outside the temple. A single thick black brush contour, heavily swelling and tapering, drawn in one confident sweep and left slightly ragged. Absolutely no background: bare cream paper surrounds the figure. Exactly three colours besides the black line — earth red, yellow ochre and a dull blue-grey — laid as flat unmodulated washes, with a single darker wash along one edge of each limb to give it roundness. Rounded, swollen, sculptural forms. Almost no interior detail: no folds, no pattern, no texture. One or two figures filling the whole sheet, the pose exaggerated for comedy, the humour affectionate rather than cruel. Crude, fast and confident. Subject:
kalighat.constraints: Watercolour on plain cream paper. The cream paper fills the entire image from edge to edge — it is not a sheet resting on a table or any other surface, and there is no dark ground, no border, no margin and no shadow anywhere around it. No background, no scenery, no frame. Only three colours plus black. No fine detail, no cross-hatching, no stippling, no airbrush, no digital gradient, no photographic realism, no 3D render. No text, no lettering, no signature, no watermark.

engraving.style: A nineteenth-century steel-plate line engraving, monochrome, warm black ink on buff paper, in the manner of the Daniells' Oriental Scenery and the Illustrated London News. Tone made entirely of fine ruled hatching and cross-hatching, with stipple for soft texture; no washes and no solid grey. Confident thin burin lines that swell slightly through the middle. Figures small and at middle distance. Subject:
engraving.constraints: Monochrome line engraving only. No colour whatsoever. No photograph, no 3D render, no digital shading, no airbrush. No text, no lettering, no signature, no watermark.

security-print.style: A specimen of Government of India security printing of the 1920s, reproduced flat and square-on: fine intaglio line engraving with guilloche and engine-turned rosette ornament, an engraved vignette set in a decorative frame, printed in one ink on lightly aged paper. Crisp die-struck line detail, tone made only of engraved lines and stipple. Centred, isolated on a plain white background, with a clean edge and no shadow. Subject:
security-print.constraints: Every panel, cartouche, ribbon, banner and label area is completely BLANK — no text, no letters, no numerals, no inscriptions, no denominations, no dates, no monograms, no fake writing or squiggles standing in for writing. Flat and square-on: no perspective, no tilt, no drop shadow, no desk, no hand, no background scene. No photographic realism beyond the printed specimen itself, no 3D render, no gradient fill, no signature, no watermark.

isolated.style: A single object or mark on a sheet of paper, photographed flat and square-on from directly above, filling most of the sheet. The paper is bare, plain and lightly aged: nothing else appears on it at all — no printing, no frame, no border, no ornament, no letterhead, no engraved device, no certificate, no caption. Just the one thing, alone on the page. Subject:
isolated.constraints: Every panel, band, slot and field within the object is completely BLANK — no text, no letters, no numerals, no dates, no monograms, no fake writing or squiggles standing in for writing. Absolutely no decorative frame, no engraved border, no guilloche, no security printing, no surrounding ornament of any kind. Matte and flat: no gloss, no specular highlight, no 3D render, no drop shadow, no perspective, no tilt, no desk, no hand, no fingers. No signature, no watermark.

environment.style: A warm, matte, painted-photographic view of an interior or camp in British India in the 1920s, lit by a single practical light source. Deep focus, sharp throughout, seen from the point of view of a person seated at the desk looking down and a little forward. Rich material detail — polished teak, worn leather, brass, cotton, dust. Subject:
environment.constraints: The middle of the frame is CLEAR AND EMPTY — a bare expanse of desk or table top where papers will be laid, with nothing on it. No text, no lettering, no signage, no writing on any paper, no titles on books. No people, no hands, no faces. Nothing modern. No lens flare, no bokeh, no shallow depth of field, no heavy vignette obscuring the corners, no watermark.
